slides.title: Template Specialization Fundamentals
slides.prompt: Template specialization allows customizing implementation for specific data types. Full (explicit) specialization overrides the template for an exact type, while partial specialization modifies behavior for a family of types (e.g. pointers or specific parameter combinations).

slides.title: Full Specialization Syntax
slides.prompt: Fill in the empty angle brackets required for full explicit template specialization.

slides.title: Function Template Partial Specialization Rule
slides.prompt: Does standard C++ allow partial specialization of function templates?
options: No, function templates cannot be partially specialized; function overloading or class templates must be used instead
Yes, function templates support partial specialization identically to class templates
Yes, but only if constexpr is applied
Only in C++20 and later standards
slides.correctAnswer: No, function templates cannot be partially specialized; function overloading or class templates must be used instead

slides.title: Partial Specialization for Pointer Types
slides.prompt: Fill in the specialized template parameter syntax for pointer types T*.

slides.title: Class Template Partial Specialization
slides.prompt: Given template <typename T, typename U> class Pair;, which syntax correctly partially specializes for cases where both arguments are the same type?
options: template <typename T, typename T> class Pair { ... };

slides.title: Full Specialization Function Template
slides.prompt: Fill in the specialized function declaration header for std::string.

slides.title: Specialization vs Overloading
slides.prompt: How does C++ compiler select between a non-template function overload and a fully specialized function template?
options: Normal non-template functions are preferred over template specializations during overload resolution
Template specializations are always preferred over normal non-template functions
It results in an ambiguous call compile error
Selection depends on the order of header includes
slides.correctAnswer: Normal non-template functions are preferred over template specializations during overload resolution

slides.title: Const Type Partial Specialization
slides.prompt: Fill in the specialization argument to specialize a class template for const types.

slides.title: Primary Template Requirement
slides.prompt: What happens if you declare a template specialization without defining a primary template first?
options: Compilation error; a primary template must be declared prior to any specialization
The compiler creates an implicit primary template automatically
The specialization becomes a standalone non-template class
It works only for full specializations
slides.correctAnswer: Compilation error; a primary template must be declared prior to any specialization
